_metadata.independence: I read only u12-blind-input.json; no other file, search, web lookup or API was used.

hints.reason: Reaches CASTLE only through the phrase/film 'castle in the sky' while MOON is simply something in the sky; the castle side is a phrase a player may not land on.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; the moon side is immediate and 'castle in the sky' is a known phrase, so it is a fair stretch rather than filler.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair wants a shared-scene word (a moonlit castle silhouette) rather than a location word.

hints.reason: The Disney castle logo/Cinderella Castle gives CASTLE and Mickey Mouse gives MOUSE; one brand, both sides instant.

best_available.why: Brand route that lands both words for virtually any player.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent single hint.

hints.reason: Torches line castle walls and torches are lit at night, so the scene exists, but neither side is a direct hit and TORCH points at many other things first.
Dracula's castle is the iconic castle and Dracula is the creature of the night; one story carries both words.

best_available.why: A single familiar story that names both the castle and the night-dwelling vampire.

pairs.pair_note: DRACULA is strong; TORCH is a plausible shared scene but diffuse.

hints.reason: Sandcastle is a compound for CASTLE and sand is the ocean beach for OCEAN; the shared beach scene is immediate.

best_available.why: Compound on one side, shared beach scene on the other; both broad.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: A fort is a near-synonym of a castle, and pirates attacking or holding a Caribbean fort (Pirates of the Caribbean, pirate-fort toy sets) is a recognizable scene.

best_available.why: Castle side is near-certain; pirate side is a familiar film/toy scene.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the strength of the pirate-fort scene; a second opinion on whether FORT is too close to a synonym of CASTLE is reasonable.

hints.reason: A castle is the royal residence and a queen is royalty; shared property that reaches both words directly.
The throne room sits inside the castle and the queen sits on the throne; one object ties both.

best_available.why: More concrete than ROYAL while reaching both words equally well.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; THRONE is the more specific image.

hints.reason: A moat is unmistakably castle; it reaches RING only through the shape idea that a moat rings the castle, which a player must reconstruct.

best_available.why: Only hint; the ring-shaped-moat route is real but a shape stretch rather than a named connection.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The ring side needs a stronger route (e.g. a story that has both a castle and a ring).

hints.reason: Toy robot is a classic toy and toy castles (playsets, building-brick castles) are common; shared-category route reaching both.

best_available.why: Both words are everyday toys; the castle side is slightly less automatic.

pairs.pair_note: Weak PASS on a shared-category route; defensible under the rubric's shared-property allowance.

hints.reason: Castles are built of stone and stone is a near-synonym of rock; both sides immediate, though the rock side is essentially a synonym.
A castle perched on a cliff is a familiar image and a cliff is a rock face; the castle side depends on that image.

best_available.why: Reaches both words without any scene-building, despite being close to a synonym of ROCK.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; flag STONE if synonym-of-target is a house rule.

hints.reason: Rose garden is a compound and castle grounds have formal gardens; the castle side is secondary but recognizable.
Beauty and the Beast: the Beast's castle and the enchanted rose; one story carries both words.

best_available.why: Story route in which castle and rose are both central objects.

pairs.pair_note: BEAST is the standout.

hints.reason: Sea salt is a compound for SALT, but the castle side relies only on castles standing by the sea (or sandcastles), which is not a named route.

best_available.why: Only hint; the salt side is a compound, the castle side is scenery.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The castle side needs a concrete tie.

hints.reason: A tower is a castle part, but reaching SHADOW requires inventing 'a tall tower casts a shadow', which is not a recognizable connection.

best_available.why: Only hint; serves the castle side only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The pair needs a word that itself evokes shadow (dark, gothic scene) and a castle.

hints.reason: Moat is pure castle, and the shark-infested moat is a well-worn villain/cartoon trope that makes the shark side recognizable.

best_available.why: Castle side certain; shark side rides a familiar trope.

pairs.pair_note: Passes on the shark-in-the-moat trope; a reviewer who does not know the trope would call it BORDERLINE.

hints.reason: A dungeon is castle through and through, but snakes in a dungeon is a looser pit trope than cobwebs or rats; the snake side needs the player to imagine it.

best_available.why: Only hint; castle side is certain and the snake-pit image is plausible.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Snake side is weaker than the spider version of the same hint.

hints.reason: Castle dungeon on one side; the cobwebbed, spider-filled dungeon is the stock image on the other.

best_available.why: Shared stock scene; the spider side is a standard set dressing.

pairs.pair_note: Weak PASS; cobwebs are the real bridge.

hints.reason: Castle gardens and gardens blooming in spring are both real, but neither side is a direct route; GARDEN points at many things before either target.

best_available.why: Only hint; both sides are soft associations.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both sides are atmospheric rather than named.

hints.reason: The Disney logo is a castle with a shooting star arcing over it, and 'Wish Upon a Star' is Disney's anthem; both words sit in one image.

best_available.why: A single logo contains both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Hogwarts Castle and the Hogwarts Express; both words are headline features of the same story.

best_available.why: Story route with both words as named objects.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: A moat is the water around a castle; both words are the definition.

best_available.why: Definitionally both words.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Hogwarts is a castle and a school of witchcraft; both words are intrinsic.
The Wicked Witch is central to Oz and her castle is a key set piece, though Emerald City competes for the castle slot.

best_available.why: Both words are named features of one place.

pairs.pair_note: HOGWARTS is clearly stronger; OZ passes on the witch's castle scene.

hints.reason: Dracula's castle is iconic, and the howling wolves he calls 'children of the night' are a recognizable part of the story and its films.

best_available.why: Story route; wolf side depends on remembering the howling wolves.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; the wolf side is secondary within the story.

hints.reason: A lion is a big cat, and the lion as 'king of beasts' (Lion King, heraldic crowned lion) gives CROWN.

best_available.why: Cat side is category membership; crown side is the king-of-beasts image.

pairs.pair_note: Good single hint.

hints.reason: Cat's-eye is a compound for CAT, but EYE reaches DIAMOND only via 'cat's-eye is also a gemstone', an explanation invented to rescue the diamond side.

best_available.why: Only hint; serves the cat side only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Needs a word that is itself a jewel or jewel-brand idea on the cat side.

hints.reason: Cat and dog are the two archetypal pets; the shared category is immediate.
'Raining cats and dogs' names both words in one idiom.
'Fight like cats and dogs', plus catfight and dogfight as compounds; both words reached by idiom.

best_available.why: Most reliable; RAIN is the most elegant idiom route.

pairs.pair_note: All three pass; RAIN and FIGHT are idiom routes, PET is category.

hints.reason: Both creatures are defined by their claws; shared physical property reaching both words.

best_available.why: Shared property true of both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Eggs in a basket (Easter, 'all your eggs in one basket') for EGG; a kitten curled in a basket is a familiar image for CAT.

best_available.why: Egg side is idiomatic; cat side is a recognizable picture.

pairs.pair_note: Weak PASS; the cat side is scene-based.

hints.reason: The hearth is the fireplace for FIRE and the cat curled by the hearth is the classic cosy scene for CAT.

best_available.why: Shared domestic scene; HEARTH is a slightly old-fashioned word.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; recognizability only moderate because HEARTH is literary.

hints.reason: Contains both target words verbatim; a rule failure regardless of how well the compound fits.
Tuna is a fish and the stereotypical cat food; both words in one object.
Fishbowl is a compound for FISH, and the cat staring into the fishbowl (or eating from its bowl) gives CAT.

best_available.why: Both words reached directly by one food.

pairs.pair_note: CATFISH must be removed as a contains_target failure; TUNA is excellent.

hints.reason: The black cat and the ghost are both stock Halloween icons; one holiday carries both.

best_available.why: Shared iconography.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Marbles are glass for GLASS, and the cat's-eye marble is the best-known marble type for CAT; the cat side needs that specific knowledge.
A window is glass for GLASS, and the cat sitting in the window is one of the most familiar cat images for CAT.

best_available.why: Broader than MARBLE; the cat-in-the-window scene needs no special knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; MARBLE is clever but moderate recognizability.

hints.reason: Goldfish is a compound for GOLD and catfish (or cats eating fish) gives CAT; two compounds on one word.

best_available.why: Double compound, both broad.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Purr is pure cat; there is no familiar phrase or scene linking purring to HEART beyond a vague 'warms the heart' explanation.

best_available.why: Only hint; serves the cat side only.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Needs a word such as a shared affection/love route or a named character.

hints.reason: Cats lick themselves and their paws for CAT; honey is licked off a spoon or paw for HONEY, but that side is a verb applicable to any food.

best_available.why: Only hint; verb route is real but the honey side is weak.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The honey side wants a sweeter-specific route.

hints.reason: Horses live in stables for HORSE; the barn/stable cat is a familiar fixture for CAT.
Wildcat and wild horse are both ordinary compounds; reaches both equally.

best_available.why: Symmetric compound route.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass.

hints.reason: 'Cool cat' is a familiar phrase for CAT and cool is the property of ice ('ice cool') for ICE.

best_available.why: Phrase on one side, property on the other, both broad.

pairs.pair_note: Good.

hints.reason: Black cat is a strong compound for CAT; the iron side rests on cast/wrought iron being black, a colour association rather than a named route.

best_available.why: Only hint; cat side certain, iron side is a colour association.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Colour route is thin on the iron side.

hints.reason: Piano keys give KEY directly; the cat walking across or playing the piano (Keyboard Cat, countless videos) gives CAT.

best_available.why: Key side certain; cat side a widely seen meme/scene.

pairs.pair_note: Passes; the cat side leans on internet culture.

hints.reason: A lion is a big cat and the king of beasts (The Lion King); both words direct.

best_available.why: Category plus title; both broad.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent.

hints.reason: Puss is simply another word for cat; KNIGHT is reached only by casting Puss in Boots as a sword-wielding hero, who is a swashbuckler rather than a knight.

best_available.why: Only hint; the Puss in Boots hero image is the sole knight route.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Cat side is a synonym; knight side is a stretch.

hints.reason: Cat's eyes are a strong cat image, but reaching LIGHT requires the player to add 'eyes glow in / reflect light', which is an explanation rather than a named route.
Cats chasing the laser pointer dot is universal for CAT, and a laser is a beam of light for LIGHT.

best_available.why: One familiar scene that is literally light and literally cat.

pairs.pair_note: LASER is excellent; EYES is a stretch on the light side.
